key_insight: Online Reasoning Calibration (ORCA) uses test-time training plus conformal prediction to recalibrate the LLM sampling process, enabling trustworthy reasoning with far fewer expensive samples. This yields generalizable, coverage-aware outputs without large compute overhead.
problem_solved: Addresses miscalibration of post-trained LLMs and uncalibrated sampling methods that force expensive test-time scaling (many samples) to achieve reliable multi-step reasoning.
method: Perform lightweight test-time training to adapt model behavior on incoming tasks/data distribution.
Apply conformal prediction techniques to the sampling pipeline to produce calibrated confidence/coverage guarantees and decide sampling effort adaptively.
Adjust sampling strategy (e.g., sample count, selection or reweighting) based on online calibration signals to reduce redundant compute while maintaining accuracy.
impact: Enables practitioners to get reliable, confidence-aware LLM reasoning with significantly less sampling cost and better generalization across tasks—improving efficiency and trustworthiness in deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input prompt → test-time trainer → conformal calibrator → adaptive sampler → calibrated answer
Bar chart comparing compute (number of samples / FLOPs) vs reasoning accuracy/coverage: baseline vs ORCA
Calibration (reliability) curve or histogram showing improved alignment of confidence with empirical accuracy
Icon set: clock/compute savings, shield/confidence, and LLM/brain to symbolize efficient, reliable reasoning
paper_title: Online Reasoning Calibration: Test-Time Training Enables Generalizable Conformal LLM Reasoning
paper_authors: Cai Zhou, Zekai Wang, Menghua Wu, Qianyu Julie Zhu, Flora C. Shi
